Subject: Pilot affordability roadmap + open asks (batching/caching TCO)

Hi Anna — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the proposed affordability roadmap so we can align with procurement.

Key pain points you shared
- Rising inference spend on payments QA workflows (rule-check + NLP enrichment)
- Latency sensitivity for fraud-review assist (target P95 < 400ms)
- Procurement needs a predictable pilot price and clear levers to reduce run rate if volume spikes

North-star goals for the pilot
- Validate that Redwood can run the payments QA flows within 400ms P95 and at or below a pilot budget of $60k total for 3 months
- Show unit economics at scale (per-1k-token) with batching + KV prefix caching enabled
- Deliver a simple ROI slide comparing current CPU-based inference and Redwood-hosted inference after batching/quantization savings

Affordability roadmap (high level)
1) Baseline measurement (week 0): capture token distribution, peak RPS, and sample prompts — we will send a brief token profile request
2) Pilot config (months 1–3): canary on 1 model variant, continuous batching, prefix caching on frequent templates, and conservative quantization (if acceptable)
3) Monitoring & gating: token-level cost dashboard + automated fallback to smaller model when budget threshold hit

Immediate asks for ClearPay (so we can finalize the affordability model):
- Confirm expected weekly token volume range (rough ballpark is fine: min / typical / peak)
- Confirm procurement timeline and whether $60k / 3 months is a hard ceiling or a target
- Any compliance/contract must-haves (e.g., PO required before start, DSAR/retention terms)

I attached a lightweight pilot_affordability_model.xlsx and a one-pager on batching assumptions. Ben — I flagged two cells for you to double-check on the batching efficiency assumptions.

Proposed next step: 30-min procurement sync next Tue 3/16 or Wed 3/17. Which works for you, Anna?

Thanks,

Hi Anna, quick technical notes and ballpark economics based on the token profile you shared on the call:

Short answers to your numbered questions:
1) Expected cost per 1k tokens (ballpark)
- Minimal config (no caching, small batch size): ~$0.20–$0.35 per 1k tokens
- With continuous batching + template-aware prefix caching: ~$0.08–$0.15 per 1k tokens
- Aggressive quantization + larger batching (for background enrichment only): ~$0.04–$0.09 per 1k tokens
2) Conservative int8 quant (recommended for non-sensitive enrichment) typically reduces inference compute by ~20–40% vs fp16 on supported models — translate that to the lower end of the ranges above (e.g., 0.08 -> ~0.05–0.06 per 1k tokens)
3) Implementation blockers
- Network: we just need a secure egress path and an allowlist for our ingestion endpoints; VPC peering optional for Private deployments
- Data: sample prompts with PII redaction are ideal; we can run a small synthetic tokenization pass if you prefer not to share customer text

How we arrive at the numbers (very high level)
- Continuous batching amortizes per-call overhead across many tokens; effective batch size is driven by RPS and latency SLOs. For your interactive stream (P95 < 400ms) we'll target dynamic batching windows tuned to hit that SLO.
- Prefix/KV caching prevents re-computation of repeated templates (typical payment templates have high repetition), which reduces token compute dramatically for repeated prompts.

Model & pilot sizing example (using your median 500k tokens/week):
- Scenario A (conservative): 500k tokens/wk -> ~2M tokens/month -> at $0.12/1k tokens = ~$240/month (compute only) — this is illustrative; other line items (storage, networking, protection) add to TCO
- Scenario B (with caching + batching): 2M tokens/month effective -> effective billable tokens drop by ~35–60% depending on repeat rates -> monthly compute ~ $100–$150 -> 3-month pilot compute ~$300–$450 (note: these figures exclude baseline platform/seat/retention fees)

I've updated the pilot_affordability_model.xlsx with a per-1k-token sensitivity table and two capped-budget scenarios that include automated throttles and model fallbacks to keep spend below $60k. See tab "BudgetScenarios". Also included is redwood_batching_onepager.pdf that explains the assumptions.

If you'd like, we can switch to a commit-based pricing proposal for the pilot (fixed $ for a known token bucket + overage pricing) so procurement has a single number to approve.
